paragraphs: Headquartered in Louisville, Kentucky, Humana Inc. and its subsidiaries, referred to throughout this document as "we," "us," "our," the "Company" or "Humana," is committed to putting health first – for our teammates, our customers, and our company. Through our Humana insurance services, and our CenterWell health care services, we make it easier for the millions of people we serve to achieve their best health – delivering the care and service they need, when they need it. These efforts are leading to a better quality of life for Medicare and Medicaid participants, families, individuals, military service personnel, and communities at large.

As of December 31, 2025, we had approximately 15 million members in our medical benefit plans, as well as approximately 4.7 million members in our specialty products. During 2025, 83% of our total premiums and services revenue were derived from contracts with the federal government, including 14% derived from our individual Medicare Advantage contracts in Florida with the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, or CMS, under which we provided health insurance coverage to approximately 1.0 million members as of December 31, 2025.

Humana Inc. was organized as a Delaware corporation in 1964. Our principal executive offices are located at 101 East Main Street, Louisville, Kentucky 40202, the telephone number at that address is (502) 580-1000, and our website address is www.humana.com. We have made available free of charge through the Investor Relations section of our web site our annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q, current reports on Form 8-K, proxy statements, and, if applicable, amendments to those reports filed or furnished pursuant to Section 13(a) of the Exchange Act, as soon as reasonably practicable after we electronically file such material with, or furnish it to, the Securities and Exchange Commission.

This Annual Report on Form 10-K, or 2025 Form 10-K, contains both historical and forward-looking information. See Part I, Item 1A, "Risk Factors" of this Form 10-K for a description of a number of factors that may adversely affect our results or business.

Our two reportable segments, Insurance and CenterWell, are based on a combination of the type of health plan customer and adjacent businesses centered on well-being solutions for our health plans and other customers. Our Chief Executive Officer, the Chief Operating Decision Maker, utilizes these segment groupings and results of each segment, measured by income (loss) from operations, to assess performance and allocate resources primarily during our annual budget process and periodic forecast updates. Our medical and specialty insurance products allow members to access health care services primarily through our networks of health care providers with whom we have contracted. These products may vary in the degree to which members have coverage. Health maintenance organizations, or HMOs, include comprehensive managed care benefits generally through a participating network of physicians, hospitals, and other providers. Preferred provider organizations, or PPOs, provide members the freedom to choose any health care provider. However, PPOs generally require the member to pay a greater portion of the provider's fee in the event the member chooses not to use a provider participating in the PPO's network. Point of Service, or POS, plans combine the advantages of HMO plans with the flexibility of PPO plans. In general, POS plans allow members to choose, at the time medical services are needed, to seek care from a provider within the plan's network or outside the network. In addition, we offer services to our health plan members as well as to third parties that promote health and wellness, including pharmacy solutions, primary care, and home solutions, as well as services and capabilities to advance population health. At the core of our strategy is our integrated care delivery model, which unites quality care, high member engagement, and sophisticated data analytics. Three core elements of the model are to improve the consumer experience by simplifying the interaction with us, engaging members in clinical programs, and offering assistance to providers in transitioning from a fee-for-service, or FFS, to a value-based arrangement. Our approach to primary, physician-directed care for our members aims to provide quality care that is consistent, integrated, cost-effective, and member-focused. The model is designed to improve health outcomes and affordability for individuals and for the health system as a whole, while offering our members a simple, seamless healthcare experience. The discussion that follows describes the products offered by each of our segments.

We have participated in the Medicare program for private health plans for over 30 years and have established a national presence, offering at least one type of Medicare plan in all 50 states. We have a geographically diverse membership base that we believe provides us with greater ability to expand our network of PPO and HMO providers. We employ strategies including health assessments and clinical guidance programs such as lifestyle and fitness programs for seniors to guide Medicare beneficiaries in making cost-effective decisions with respect to their health care. We believe these strategies result in cost savings that occur from making positive behavior changes.

headings: As a government contractor, we are exposed to risks that may materially adversely affect our business or our willingness or ability to participate in government health care programs.

Any failure by us to manage acquisitions, divestitures and other significant transactions successfully may have a material adverse effect on our results of operations, financial position, and cash flows.
If we fail to develop and maintain satisfactory relationships with the providers of care to our members, our business may be adversely affected.
paragraphs: If we do not design and price our products properly and competitively, if the premiums we charge are insufficient to cover the cost of health care services delivered to our members, if we are unable to implement clinical initiatives to provide a better health care experience for our members, lower costs and appropriately document the risk profile of our members, or if our estimates of benefits expense are inadequate, our profitability may be materially adversely affected. We estimate the costs of our benefits expense payments, and design and price our products accordingly, using actuarial methods and assumptions based upon, among other relevant factors, claim payment patterns, medical cost inflation, and historical developments such as claim inventory levels and claim receipt patterns. These estimates involve extensive judgment, and have considerable inherent variability because they are extremely sensitive to changes in claim payment patterns and medical cost trends. Accordingly, our reserves may be insufficient.

We use a substantial portion of our revenues to pay the costs of health care services delivered to our members, including claims payments, capitation payments to providers (predetermined amounts paid to cover services), estimates of future payments to hospitals and others for medical care provided to our members, and various other costs. Generally, premiums in the health care business are fixed for one-year periods. Accordingly, costs we incur in excess of our benefit cost projections generally are not recovered in the contract year through higher premiums. We estimate the costs of our future benefit claims and other expenses using actuarial methods and assumptions based upon claim payment patterns, medical inflation, historical developments, including claim inventory levels and claim receipt patterns, and other relevant factors. We also record benefits payable for future payments. We continually review estimates of future payments relating to benefit claims costs for services incurred in the current and prior periods and make necessary adjustments to our reserves, including premium deficiency reserves where appropriate. However, these estimates involve extensive judgment, and have considerable inherent variability that is sensitive to claim payment patterns and medical cost trends. Many factors may and often do cause actual health care costs to exceed what was estimated and used to set our premiums. These factors may include:
•increased use of medical facilities and services, and the increased cost of such services;
•increased use or cost of prescription drugs, including specialty prescription drugs; •the introduction of new or costly treatments, prescription drugs, or new technologies;
•variances in actual versus estimated levels of cost associated with new products, benefits or lines of business, product changes or benefit level changes;
•changes in the demographic characteristics of an account or market;

Our industry relies on two key statistics to measure performance. The benefit ratio, which is computed by taking total benefits expense as a percentage of premiums revenue, represents a statistic used to measure underwriting profitability. The operating cost ratio, which is computed by taking total operating costs, excluding depreciation and amortization, as a percentage of total revenue less investment income, represents a statistic used to measure administrative spending efficiency.

paragraphs: 總部設於肯塔基州路易維爾市，Humana Inc. 及其子公司，於本文件中稱為 "we," "us," "our," "本公司" 或 "Humana," 堅持以健康為首要考量 – 為我們的員工、客戶及公司。透過我們的 Humana 保險服務，以及 CenterWell 醫療服務，我們讓服務的數百萬人更容易達成最佳健康 – 提供他們所需之照護與服務，於他們需要之時。這些努力正引導 Medicare 和 Medicaid 參與者、家庭、個人、軍事服務人員及廣大社區獲得更優質的生活品質。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們在醫療福利計畫中擁有約 1500 萬名成員，以及在專門產品中擁有約 470 萬名成員。2025 年，我們總計的 premiums 和 services 收入中，約有 83% 來自與聯邦政府的契約，其中包括 14% 來自我們在佛羅裏達州與 Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, 或 CMS，簽訂的個人 Medicare Advantage 契約，根據這些契約，我們為約 100 萬名成員提供健康保險覆蓋，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日。

我們的醫療與專門保險產品允許成員透過我們與之簽約的醫療服務提供者網路來取得醫療服務。這些產品在成員的覆蓋程度上可能有所不同。健康維護組織，或 HMOs，通常透過參與的醫生、醫院及其他提供者網路提供全面的管理式醫療福利。優先提供者組織，或 PPOs，讓成員有自由選擇任何醫療服務提供者。然而，PPOs 通常要求成員在選擇不使用 PPO 網路內的提供者時，需支付較高的提供者費用。點數服務，或 POS，計畫結合 HMO 計畫的優點與 PPO 計畫的靈活性。一般而言，POS 計畫允許成員在需要醫療服務時，選擇在計畫的網路內或網路外的提供者。此外，我們為健康計畫成員及第三方提供促進健康與 wellness 的服務，包括藥物解決方案、門診照護與居家解決方案，以及促進人口健康的服務與能力。我們策略的核心是我們的整合式照護交付模式，該模式結合了品質照護、高成員參與度與先進的數據分析。該模式的三個核心要素是透過簡化與我們的互動、參與臨牀計畫及協助提供者從費用支付模式（FFS）轉向價值型安排，來改善消費者體驗。我們對成員的門診、醫生導向照護方法旨在提供一致、整合、成本效益且以成員為中心的品質照護。此模式設計用以改善個人與整體醫療系統的健康結果與負擔，同時為成員提供簡單、無縫的醫療體驗。以下討論說明各分部所提供的產品。

我們產業依賴兩個關鍵指標來衡量績效。受益比率，其計算方式為總受益費用佔 premiums 收入的百分比，用以衡量承保獲利能力。營運成本比率，其計算方式為總營運成本（扣除折舊及攤銷）佔總收入減去投資收入的百分比，用以衡量行政開支效率。

headings: 與本公司業務相關的風險
作為政府承包商，我們面臨可能對本公司業務或參與政府醫療衛生計畫之意願或能力產生重大不利影響的風險。
若本公司未能成功管理併購、資產處置及其他重大交易，可能對本公司營運成果、財務狀況及現金流產生重大不利影響。
若本公司未能發展並維持與會員照護提供者之間滿意的關係，可能對本公司業務產生不利影響。
paragraphs: 若我們未能適當且具競爭力地設計與訂價產品，若我們所收取的費用不足以彌補提供給會員的醫療服務成本，若我們無法實施臨牀方案以提供更好的醫療體驗給會員、降低成本並恰當記錄會員的風險資料，或若我們對福利費用的預估不足，則我們的獲利能力可能受到重大不利影響。我們使用精算方法與假設，根據包括聲請給付模式、醫療成本通貨膨脹及歷史發展（如聲請給付庫存量與聲請給付接收模式）等相關因素，來估算我們的福利費用支出，並據此設計與訂價產品。這些預估涉及廣泛的判斷，且具有相當大的內在變動性，因為它們對聲請給付模式與醫療成本趨勢的變動極為敏感。因此，我們的準備金可能不足。

我們將相當大一部分的營業收入用來支付提供給會員的醫療服務成本，包括聲請給付、對提供者（預先確定的費用用以覆蓋服務）的資本支付、對醫院及其他機構預估未來提供給會員的醫療服務費用，以及各種其他成本。通常，醫療服務業的 premiums（費用）在一年期間為固定。因此，我們在合約年度內所產生的費用若超過我們的福利費用預估，通常無法透過提高 premiums（費用）來補償。我們使用精算方法與假設，根據聲請給付模式、醫療通貨膨脹、歷史發展（包括聲請給付庫存量與聲請給付接收模式）及其他相關因素，來估算我們未來的福利聲請費用及其他費用。我們也會記錄未來支付的福利費用。我們持續審查與當前及過去期間所提供的服務相關的未來支付預估，並根據需要調整我們的準備金，包括 premiums（費用）不足準備金（premium deficiency reserves）在適當的情況下。然而，這些預估涉及廣泛的判斷，且具有相當大的內在變動性，這一點對聲請給付模式與醫療成本趨勢的變動極為敏感。許多因素可能導致實際的醫療服務成本高於預估的數值，並用來設定我們的 premiums（費用）。這些因素可能包括：
•醫療設施與服務的使用增加，以及這些服務的成本增加；
•處方藥的使用或成本增加，包括專門處方藥；•新治療方式、處方藥或新技術的推出；
•與新產品、福利或業務線、產品變更或福利層級變更相關的實際成本與預估成本之間的差異；
•帳戶或市場的人口統計特徵變動；
